name: Access: role permissions, venue requests, partner presale
description: Who may do what, set by the organization. **Role API permissions**: the owner chooses which scopes each role's API keys and personal / OAuth tokens may carry, within a fixed ceiling per role; every credential is held to it at each request, so lowering a role applies at once. **Venue requests**: a venue another organization runs on Exos can't take your events or holds directly (403 `venue_approval_required`, with `venue_id` and `request_endpoint`); send its organization a booking request, and once approved it shares the event with you with the scopes it chooses (co-hosted events). The event stays the venue's: it sells, refunds and settles as their other events. **Partner presale**: whether distribution partners may sell during a member presale. Writes need an org API key (sk_live_…) whose creator holds the role named on each route.

endpoints.description: For each role: the scopes its keys and tokens may carry in this organization (`effective` for user tokens, `key_effective` for org API keys), today's `default` (tokens) and `key_default` (keys) that apply while the owner has set nothing, the `ceiling` no setting can exceed, and the owner's `configured` set (null: none). The owner always has every scope.

The owner sets which scopes a role's keys and tokens may carry, within the role's ceiling (content never gets finance or refunds; scanners stay at the door; only owners have org:admin). Takes effect on every existing key and token of that role at their next request: a scope taken away is refused at once, and giving it back restores what each key was made with (never more). `scopes: null` (or `reset: true`) goes back to the default. Needs a key created by the owner.

parameters.name: scopes
parameters.description: The scopes the role may carry (or null for the default).

parameters.name: reset
parameters.description: true: back to the default (same as scopes: null).

responses.description: A scope above the role's ceiling, or a key not created by the owner.

example.error: the content role can never be given finance:read
role must be manager, finance, content or scanner (the owner always has every scope).

endpoints.description: Venues other organizations run on Exos that take booking requests, by name or city (at least 2 characters, up to 25 results), with their rooms. Never their contacts or notes. An event, hold or template at one of these venues needs that organization's approval: send a booking request.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Part of the venue's name or city, 2-100 characters.

endpoints.summary: Suggest the venue your record stands for
endpoints.description: For one of your rented or partner venues: owned venues of other organizations with the same name and city, every match listed (two are never decided for you), each with `verified` (Exos staff checked that organization runs it; it clears when that organization edits the venue's name, address or relationship). Only venues that take booking requests, as in the directory. Nothing is linked until you choose one (PUT /v1/venues/:id/listed-venue): anyone can call a venue owned, so a name match is only a suggestion.

endpoints.summary: Link your record to the venue it stands for
endpoints.description: Say that your rented or partner venue is another organization's owned venue. From then on events and holds at your record need that organization's approval (venue_approval_required), and booking requests through it go to them. The link stays: only Exos staff can remove it. Needs a key created by an owner or manager.

parameters.description: The owned venue (from the suggestions or the directory).

endpoints.description: Ask the organization that runs a venue for a date (and a room). Use this when creating an event or hold there answers 403 venue_approval_required. The venue's owners and managers approve it (a hold on their calendar, or a draft event they share with you) or decline it. One pending request per venue, room and date; at most 50 pending and 30 a day. A venue_id of your own record of the venue (a rented or partner venue linked to it) asks the venue it stands for. An Idempotency-Key makes a retry return the first request. Needs a key created by an owner or manager.

parameters.name: venue_id
parameters.description: The venue (from /v1/venue-directory, or the venue_id in a venue_approval_required answer).

parameters.name: room_id
parameters.description: A room of that venue (default: the whole venue).

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The night, in the venue's calendar: today or later.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: For the venue, at most 2000 characters.

endpoints.description: The venue's side. Puts the night on your calendar as a hold (create=hold, the default) or a hold converted into a draft event of your organization at the venue (create=event), and decides what the requester may do on that event: `scopes`, from events:read, events:write, tickets:read and finance:read (default events:read, events:write, tickets:read; events:write brings events:read). Refunds are never shared: the event is yours and sells, refunds and settles like your other events. With create=hold, the grant starts when you convert the hold. Only a pending request (409 otherwise). Needs a key created by an owner or manager.

parameters.name: scopes
parameters.description: What the requester may do on the event.

parameters.name: time
parameters.description: With create=event: start, HH:MM venue-local (default the request's start_time, else 20:00).

parameters.name: capacity
parameters.description: With create=event: the ticket type's size (default the room, else the venue).

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: The hold's level in that night's line (default last).

responses.description: A user token, or an API key whose creator is not an owner or manager of the organization now.
